messages:
Ana (CSM): Quick weekly health check for AcmeCorp — spike in error rate this week, need triage. summary: 5xx up 3.8% -> 9.2% total requests, timeouts up 40%, several rate-limited clients. Top failing endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat/stream, /v1/embeddings. sending graphs in thread. @Ethan can you sanity-check?
Ethan (SRE): Looking. I see correlated latency at 2026-03-09T02:00Z and again 2026-03-11T15:00Z. Errors look like 503 gateway + upstream timeouts. attaching quick log excerpt.
Ethan (SRE): ```
2026-03-11T15:03:12Z svc-proxy req_id=abc123 upstream_err=EOF route=/v1/generate status=503 latency_ms=12045
2026-03-11T15:03:12Z svc-worker model=llama2 variant=q4_kv timeout=10s
```
Priya (Support): Customer reported "requests failing intermittently" during their batch ingest window. They mentioned hitting bursts ~450 rps. Their plan is growth to 1k rps next month — potential renewal risk if not stabilized. Kira, FYI.
Kira (Account Exec): Noted. Renewal conversation in two weeks; please flag if we need a short-term credit or dedicated burst while fix lands.
Jonas (Infra): Two quick theories: (1) autoscaler undershoot under short spikes causing queueing -> upstream timeouts; (2) token-rate limits hitting headroom leading to 429s which clients retry aggressively causing amplification.
Ethan (SRE): Agreed. Current autoscaler config has scale_cooldown=60s, target_util=0.7. For AcmeCorp traffic pattern (spiky), we should lower cooldown to 20s and allow short burst capacity + pre-warm a few instances. I'll draft change.
Ana (CSM): Are the 5xxs originating at our proxy layer or the model-worker? Which endpoints most impacted?
Ethan (SRE): Proxy shows the majority for /v1/generate (56% of 5xx), /v1/chat/stream (27%), /v1/embeddings (12%). Remaining are misc. Rate-limit 429s are concentrated on /v1/embeddings where client uses short-window parallel requests.
Priya (Support): Customer says embedding clients do parallel calls per item. We recommended batching before, but they haven't implemented. Can CS push a short guide? I can share a sample batching snippet.
Priya (Support): ```python
# suggested client-side batching
chunks = [items[i:i+64] for i in range(0, len(items), 64)]
for c in chunks:
  resp = client.embeddings.create(model="embed-128", input=c)
```
Jonas (Infra): Quick mitigations I can push now:
- lower scale_cooldown to 20s for acme-prod
- enable a small burst pool (+2 instances) for 24h while we monitor
- add a per-client soft-rate-limit header to proxy (429 after >300rps)
Ethan (SRE): I'll own the autoscaler change and burst pool. ETA 45m. I'll also add extra logging for upstream timeouts and surface sample request ids in the dashboard.
Ana (CSM): Great. Priya please send batching guide + recommended request pacing to the customer today.
Priya (Support): Will do. Also will ask for a list of their heavy keys (api keys) so we can apply soft limits per key if needed.
Kira (Account Exec): If ops change helps, we can offer a one-week elevated burst at no charge to keep them happy before renewal. Marking as potential concession.
OncallBot: Incident annotation: config_change requested by Ethan (SRE) — change_id=chg-20260311-78 queued at 1765014600
Ethan (SRE): Change applied: scale_cooldown=20s and burst_pool=+2 for acme-prod. Monitoring dashboards updated. watch: https://console.redwood/observability/acme/health
Ethan (SRE): Early signal: 1.2% drop in 5xx in first 10m, timeouts down 18%.
Ana (CSM): Excellent. Can we get a short blurb to share in weekly report and to include in renewal brief?
Ethan (SRE): Blurb: "Applied autoscaler cooldown reduction and temporary burst capacity; observed early 1-2% reduction in 5xx and lower timeout rates. Next steps: continue monitoring for 6h, then consider permanent config tweaks or Dedicated capacity for predictable peak handling." 
Ana (CSM): I'll add that. Owners: Ethan -> infra change; Priya -> customer enablement; Jonas -> per-key rate-limit follow-up. Follow-up check in 6h. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Priya (Support): Logged action items in CS tracker: https://pm.redwood/accts/ACME/health-20260311
Ethan (SRE): FYI, if we still see noisy 429s from embeddings clients after batching, recommend we provide a client-side SDK helper that does automatic concurrency control.
Ana (CSM): Added to backlog. Closing thread after 6h checkpoint unless regressions.
